{"number":677,"title":"baselining: decide delivery on what the base branch requires, not on whether CI exists","body":"## The wrong predicate

`deliveryAction` gated on `hasPrCi` — *does any workflow trigger on `pull_request`* — as a stand-in for *does auto-merge have something to wait behind*. The two diverge on an unprotected base branch.

GitHub queues a PR only behind what the branch **requires**. A repo with a full test suite and `"protected": false` is mergeable the entire time its checks run, so `enablePullRequestAutoMerge` is rejected as `Pull request is in clean status` — exactly as it is on a repo with no CI at all. Enabling *Allow auto-merge* does not change this: the setting permits the feature; a required check is what gives it something to wait for.

Consequence on those members: the arm failed **every** cycle. #649's in-cycle landing caught it, so the PR did land — but by the fallback, while the log told the owner to go fix a setting that was never the cause.

## The fix

`mergeGatePresent` reads the base branch's `protected` flag plus the ruleset rules that apply to it (deliberately not `/branches/{base}/protection`, which wants admin the Action's `GITHUB_TOKEN` does not carry). An unreadable answer is **unknown, not absent** — unknown assumes a gate, so a gate we cannot see gets armed rather than merged past.

Three delivery shapes rather than two, because the two empty ones differ in what they leave to verify:

| base branch | tree | action |
|---|---|---|
| — | no `pull_request` workflow | `merge` — no check will ever report; nothing to wait on |
| requires nothing | PR CI present | `land` — runs are real and must still be green; only the doomed mutation is skipped |
| requires something | PR CI present | `arm`, as before |

Collapsing the middle case into `merge` would have merged unverified content on every unprotected member with a test suite — the opposite of the point.

`armFailureAdvice` and `mergeReason` gain the shape with **no remedy**: a "clean status" rejection names no setting, because sending an owner to fix something already correct is worse than saying nothing.

## The agent lane

It had no fallback at all — `task.md` §4 said arm it, and **Never** listed merging by hand. On an unprotected member the agent's arm always fails, so its PR waited for the next cycle's disposal: the same ~24h canon-to-main offset #649 removed for the worker. §4 now licenses the hand merge for exactly the "clean status" case and no other, once this cycle's checks are green; every other failed arm stays the worker's to land around.

Also: `git-github-advanced` records the portable GitHub fact (auto-merge waits on requirements, not on CI, and which endpoints answer that without admin), and sheepdog's follow no longer describes an open PR as "waiting on auto-merge" when its member has no arm to wait for.

## Verification

- Six branches mutated independently, each turning exactly its own test red.
- Full CI set **1227 passing**.
- `check_the_world`: **0 blocking**, 9 advisory (pre-existing file-placement, none on changed lines).

Refs #674

Comment class: correction (the stranded-PR failure was an execution failure, per the owner: delivery must land every time, not self-heal next cycle).

## The actual root cause — a race, not a setting

TLDR's forced run log, 2026-08-07:

```
08:00:22.67  dispatched claudinite-conformance.yml on claudinite/maintenance-…
08:00:23.44  could not arm auto-merge (clean status) … landing it here.
08:00:23.74  PR #201 not landable this cycle (no successful run on its head sha) — leaving it open
```

The #649 in-cycle landing dispatched its verification run and read the head sha **0.3 seconds later**, before the run had registered in the API — and judged the empty list as "nothing will ever verify this" (give-up) instead of "the run I just started hasn't appeared yet". Its 180s landing budget was never used; seven members' green PRs stranded in one pass. `landAttempt` now takes an `expected` count — the runs this worker itself dispatched — and treats fewer-visible-than-dispatched as *poll*, bounded exactly as before.

## Absorbing #677's insight, rebuilt for the current tree

The arm predicate moves from "does PR CI exist" to "does the base branch **require** anything" — `branch.protected` plus the ruleset rules applying to it (never `/branches/{base}/protection`, which wants admin); an unreadable answer is **unknown, never absent**. Three delivery shapes:

| base branch | tree | action |
|---|---|---|
| — | no `pull_request` workflow | `merge` — nothing will ever report |
| requires nothing | PR CI present | `land` — skip the doomed clean-status arm; wait for this cycle's dispatched runs, merge on their green |
| requires something, or unknown | PR CI present | `arm`, with the landing pass as fallback |

Also from #677, adapted: `mergeReason` stops prescribing "Allow auto-merge" for the shape with no remedy; the agent lane in task.md licenses a hand merge for exactly the clean-status case once the head's checks are green (and the Never list carves that one exception); sheepdog's follow stops describing every open PR as "waiting on auto-merge" — it cannot see whether an arm exists.

Not blindly copied: #677 predates the prework rename and the three-responsibility split; this reimplements its decision table against the current worker (which #677's diff no longer applies to). Once this lands, **#677 is superseded and can close**.

## Verification

- New tests written first and watched fail (missing export / old race behavior), then green: the race (`expected` poll), the gate classifier (present/absent/unknown), the three delivery shapes, the no-false-remedy `mergeReason`.
- Full suite: **1257 pass, 0 fail**; `check_the_world`: 0 blocking.

Refs #676, #674.

An execution failure, exactly as you called it: the self-heal was compensating for a race in the very pass that was supposed to make healing unnecessary.

The fix makes delivery deterministic under these settings:

3. Once #690 lands, **#677 is superseded and can close** — its insight lives on in current code.
